'''''Yeneen''''' is an [[extinct]] genus of [[titanosauria]]n sauropod dinosaur known from the [[Late Cretaceous]] ([[Santonian]] age) [[Bajo de la Carpa Formation]] of Argentina. The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Yeneen houssayi''''', known from at least one partial skeleton. Its discovery highlights the diversity of titanosaurs in this formation, which also includes ''[[Bonitasaura]]'', ''[[Inawentu]]'', ''[[Overosaurus]]'', ''[[Rinconsaurus]]'', and ''[[Traukutitan]]''.

== Discovery and naming ==
The ''Yeneen'' fossil material was discovered in outcrops at the {{gloss|La Invernada}} site, part of the [[Bajo de la Carpa Formation]] ([[Neuquén Group]]) of Argentina. Three specimens were collected, which are housed in the Museo Municipal Argentino Urquiza. One specimen, permanently [[Accession number (cultural property)|accessioned]] as MAU-Pv-LI-538/1–30 consists of a partial [[Joint|disarticulated]] skeleton, comprising six {{dinogloss|cervicals|cervical}}, ten {{dinogloss|dorsals|dorsal}}, and one {{dinogloss|caudals|caudal}} vertebrae, in addition to the {{dinogloss|sacrum}} articulated with both {{dinogloss|ilia}}, and several {{dinogloss|ribs}}. A second specimen found in association with MAU-Pv-LI-538 but belonging to an individual of a smaller size is a single right ilium, accessioned as MAU-Pv-LI-539. A third specimen, MAU-Pv-LI-731, includes disarticulated [[Axial skeleton|axial]] and [[Appendicular skeleton|appendicular]] bones and is still undergoing [[Fossil preparation|preparation]] to better study the skeletal anatomy.<ref name="Yeneen" />

In 2026, Leonardo S. Filippi and colleagues [[Species description|described]] ''Yeneen houssayi'' as a new genus and species of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaurs based on these fossil remains, establishing MAU-Pv-LI-538 as the [[holotype]] specimen. MAU-Pv-LI-539, the isolated ilium, was assigned to [[Cf.#Biological use|cf.]] ''Yeneen houssayi'', meaning the researchers could not confidently assign it to this species based on anatomical characters shared with the holotype, but it still bears characters distinguishing it from other titanosaur taxa. MAU-Pv-LI-731 was not referred to ''Y. houssayi'' or any other taxon, pending the finalized preparation of the specimen.<ref name="Yeneen" />

The [[Genus|generic name]], ''Yeneen'', is the name of an entity in [[Tehuelche language|Tehuelche]] (Aonikenk) culture tied to the cold and winter weather. This name was chosen to reference the type locality, [[:es:Invernada en bovinos|La Invernada]], which is a Spanish word referring to the wintering location of [[cattle]]. The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]], ''houssayi'', honors [[Bernardo Houssay|Bernardo Alberto Houssay]], a recipient of the [[Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine]], who was involved in promoting the creation of the [[National Scientific and Technical Research Council]] (CONICET), an Argentinian agency that directs much of the academic scientific research performed in the country.<ref name="Yeneen" />

== Classification ==
To test the relationships and affinities of ''Yeneen'' with other titanosaurs, Filippi and colleagues developed a novel [[phylogenetic]] dataset modified from that of Filippi et al. (2024)<ref name="Inawentu" /> (the description of the coeval ''[[Inawentu]]''). These results placed ''Yeneen'' as part of the clade [[Saltasauroidea]], in a more exclusive group the researchers referred to as "Clade A", where it diverges after ''[[Narambuenatitan]]'' but before ''[[Overosaurus]]''. == Paleoecology ==
''Yeneen'' is known from the [[Bajo de la Carpa Formation]], which dates to the [[Santonian]] age of the late [[Cretaceous]] period. Its sediments represent [[fluvial]] and [[Aeolian processes|aeolian]] systems, with a semi-arid paleoenvironment.<ref name="Garrido2010" /> In addition to ''Yeneen'', several dinosaurs are known from this formation. [[Sauropods]] include the diverse fellow titanosaurs ''[[Bonitasaura]]'', ''[[Inawentu]]'', ''[[Overosaurus]]'', ''[[Rinconsaurus]]'', and ''[[Traukutitan]]''.<ref name="Yeneen" /> Theropods preserved comprise the [[megaraptorid]]s (''[[Rinconraptor]]'' and ''[[Tratayenia]]''),<ref name="Rinconraptor" /> [[abelisauroid]]s (''[[Velocisaurus]]'', ''[[Llukalkan]]'', and ''[[Viavenator]]''), [[alvarezsaurid]]s (''[[Achillesaurus]]'' and ''[[Alvarezsaurus]]''), the [[unenlagiine]] paravian ''[[Diuqin]]'', and the [[avialan]]s (birds, in the broad sense) ''[[Neuquenornis]]'' and ''[[Patagopteryx]]''. Other reptiles include the [[elasmaria]]n ornithopod dinosaur ''[[Mahuidacursor]]'' and various non-dinosaurs, including indeterminate [[pterosaur]]s and fossil [[snake]]s (''[[Dinilysia]]''), [[lizard]]s (''[[Paleochelco]]''), [[turtle]]s (''[[Lomalatachelys]]''), and several [[crocodyliforms]].<ref name="Diuqin" />
